purpose: Requirements closed as far as the artifacts of their own gate allow, each naming the gate or slice that completes them. tools/partial_closures.py fails the build on an entry with no completer, an unknown completer, or a completer that has landed while the entry is still open.

partial_closures.why: The preview names line prices, modifiers, tax, fees and discounts. Tax resolves to config.configuration_version under category 'tax' and a discount to config.policy under category 'discount'; both are configured, non-zero and exercised. A FEE has no configuration heading before FR-CFG-001C, so ordering.charge_rule can hold one and nothing at this gate creates one. The total is a sum over the components that exist and carries no zero literal for the absent kind.
Whether a discount applies before or after tax is a bill-calculation decision. At M3-A both are computed on the line subtotal, which is the only reading that does not pre-empt FR-BIL-005.
Item, modifier, discount, tax and total snapshots persist at acceptance with the locale. The fee snapshot persists the moment a fee component exists, and no configured source produces one before M4.

A draft cart creates no order, no ledger event and no charge component, and a cart with an order against it is frozen. That a draft creates no FINANCIAL obligation is re-proved once checks and payments exist; the requirements register already dual-gates this row at M4.

Availability, hours, channel and quantity are revalidated at submission. Capacity is the fifth dimension the requirement names and it means station workload, which needs the stations and their thresholds that FR-FUL-013 builds at M3-B.
partial_closures.closed_by_evidence: ordering.revalidate_cart() gained a fifth leg at M3-B reading fulfillment.capacity_pressure(), which compares each station's live ticket count against its configured concurrent_ticket_threshold and reports the outlet's configured capacity_response. A service policy stating neither is refused, not defaulted. tests/m3b loads a station past its threshold and requires the submission to be blocked under a throttling policy and to proceed under a promise-time policy.

partial_closures.why: Add-on orders in one session are distinct aggregates with independent timestamps and independent ledgers, which is proved here. That their FULFILLMENT is independent needs tickets, which are M3-B.
partial_closures.closed_by_evidence: Tickets belong to an ORDER, and an add-on is a different order, so independent fulfillment came out of the model rather than being added to it. tests/m3b places a second order on one occupancy and requires disjoint ticket sets, independent state machines and independent timings.

partial_closures.why: Amendment emits an explicit event retaining before and after, and the window is enforced from the ordering policy. The policy can only speak in commercial states at this gate: 'after preparation has begun' is a ticket state and tickets are M3-B.
partial_closures.closed_by_evidence: ordering.amend_order_line() was replaced at M3-B (CREATE OR REPLACE; 0010 is checksum-locked) to refuse when any ticket for the order has left queued, acknowledged or held. The commercial state alone was never enough: an order can sit in a state the ordering policy permits while a station is already cooking it.

partial_closures.aspect: payment dimension of the cancellation policy
partial_closures.why: Cancellation resolves by state, channel and reason. The payment dimension needs payments to exist; the requirements register already dual-gates this row at M4.

An authorized void after acceptance records its reason and an immutable audit row. 'For an unpaid order' cannot be falsified at M3-A because no payment artifact exists to make it false, so the precondition is asserted against an empty set and must be re-proved at M4.
The timeline renders order events chronologically with the audience decided when each entry is written. Station events belong on it and do not exist until M3-B.
partial_closures.closed_by_evidence: fulfillment.apply_ticket_event() writes station milestones onto the order timeline through ordering.write_station_timeline_entry(), and ordering.rebuild_projections() was extended to replay the fulfillment ledger so those entries survive a rebuild. One timeline out of two ledgers, with the audience decided where the entry is written.

partial_closures.why: Service-request events belong on the same timeline and do not exist until M3-C.
partial_closures.closed_by_evidence: A service request keeps its own append-only ledger and its customer-visible messages are notices in notify.notice, which notify.customer_timeline() merges with the order timeline at READ time for one table session. Merged rather than written into ordering.order_timeline_entry a second time: a request for water belongs to no order, and forcing one into the order ledger would have needed an order to exist before a guest could ask for anything. tests/m3c renders that merged timeline in a browser and requires both sources in it.

partial_closures.why: The chain links four of the six artifacts the requirement names — request, cart, table session and order — and survives projection rebuild. 'fulfillment_ticket' is a label of ordering.artifact_kind with no rows until M3-B, so the later slice extends the chain rather than reshaping it.
partial_closures.closed_by_evidence: fulfillment.release_order() links each ticket into the chain through ordering.link_correlation_artifact(), so the 'fulfillment_ticket' label M3-A declared with no rows now has them. tests/m3b requires the link to survive a projection rebuild.

partial_closures.why: 'service_request' is likewise a label with no rows until M3-C.
partial_closures.closed_by_evidence: ordering.artifact_kind has carried the service_request label since M3-A with no rows; service.apply_request_event() now writes the link, from the FOLD rather than from the caller, so a rebuild restores it — the repair M3-B made after the reversed run found the ticket link could not be. tests/m3c proves every request is in the chain and that all three ledgers rebuild to identical digests.

partial_closures.aspect: service requests consolidated by a merge
partial_closures.why: A merge consolidates orders, participants, carts and allergy concerns, each move audited and counted. Service requests are the other thing the requirement says must be consolidated and they do not exist until M3-C.
partial_closures.closed_by_evidence: Service requests are bound to a table session, so a merge moves them with everything else that session owns and no separate consolidation step exists to get wrong. tests/m3c raises requests on two occupancies, merges them and requires the union with nothing lost and nothing duplicated, reusing M3-A's session census.

partial_closures.aspect: service requests preserved by a move
partial_closures.why: A move preserves session identity and every order, which is proved by inventory. Service requests are named by the requirement and do not exist until M3-C.
partial_closures.closed_by_evidence: The same property under a move: the requests travel with the session because they reference it, and tests/m3c proves the set is unchanged either side of the move.

partial_closures.why: A session cannot close over an unresolved order unless an authorized exception is recorded with a reason and an account. The FINANCIAL condition cannot be proved before checks and settlement exist; the requirements register already dual-gates this row at M4.

Order projections rebuild from the ledger and compare byte-deterministically. Financial projections arrive at M4 and rebuild after outage replay at M5a; the requirements register dual-gates this row at both.

Accepted line units route by versioned rule and a ticket records the rule version that placed it. That routing continues to work when the outlet node is authoritative is this row's revalidation at M5a, where the node exists.
All eleven states render and the seven display buckets are measured in a real browser. That the same KDS operates from the local node during an outage needs the node, which is M5a.

Allergy emphasis is measured non-colour-only on the KDS and expo surfaces, and the generated station ticket document carries its allergy lines first and in words. That the salience survives PHYSICAL printing needs the print path, which is M5a; this gate proves the document, not the paper.

A ready notice is emitted naming the ticket and the assigned waiter, and uncollected notices escalate on the configured window. Delivery is a channel and channels are FR-NOT-001 at M3-C; there is no transport, template or delivery-status column here for one to be mistaken for.
partial_closures.closed_by_evidence: M3-B emitted the ready event and left the transport open, recording it here. M3-C tells the recipient: notify.emit() resolves who should know and notify.send_pending() writes it to their in-app inbox in the language the session chose. The CHANNEL is still not built — outlet-local notices are M5a — and this gate's honest scope is the in-app one, which is what FR-NOT-001 asks for at M3.

partial_closures.why: Prep, wait and SLA times compute per station, item and order from timestamps the fold wrote out of the ledger. Consuming them as analytics is operational reporting at M6.

partial_closures.aspect: physical printing and dedup across restart
partial_closures.why: Station ticket documents are generated and deduplicated by a unique key on (ticket, revision), where the revision ignores document generation itself. Physical printing, print-agent delivery and deduplication across a restart are the local print path, which is M5a.

partial_closures.aspect: rerouting with the outlet node authoritative
partial_closures.why: An authorized reroute moves the ticket and its line units without creating anything, proved by a unit-count constraint across every live ticket for the order. Behaviour while the outlet node is authoritative is M5a's.

partial_closures.aspect: fulfillment labels derived rather than stored
partial_closures.why: A LITERAL DIVERGENCE from the pinned SM-ORDER, recorded as a decision rather than an omission. That machine lists in_fulfillment, partially_ready, ready, partially_served and served as ORDER states; migration 0010 recorded at M3-A that no fulfillment label appears on the commercial order, and M3-B keeps that. fulfillment.order_fulfillment_state() computes every one of those labels from the order's tickets, so the machine's SEMANTICS are preserved while the same fact is refused a second home that could contradict the first. tests/m3b proves each label reachable and correct and asserts against the catalog that no column in ordering could hold one. SM-ORDER's last edge — served -> completed on operational AND FINANCIAL conditions — needs checks, so this is revisited at M4.

The staff half of FR-NOT-012 says the notification centre RENDERS in English, and rendering a staff screen is staff UX, which M3-D owns. Building one here would hand M3-D a shape from the slice that does not own it — the objection raised at M2-A, M3-A and M3-B. The DATA surface is complete: notify.staff_notification_center() returns each person's own notices with their kind, class, severity, subject, body and read state, refusing anyone without an active membership at the outlet. M3-D adds a screen over finished data rather than finishing the data.

partial_closures.aspect: bill, payment, tip, outage and sync producers
partial_closures.why: FR-NOT-001 names eight classes of event. Order, kitchen and service request have producers at this gate. The other five are in notify.catalog_event with has_producer = false and notify.emit() refuses them by name, so the kinds are real and nothing pretends to raise one. Bill, payment and tip arrive at M4; outage and sync at M5a, which is recorded separately.

The routing and accountability model is complete: a critical kind reaches notify.accountable_staff(), which reads the outlet's configured role and refuses rather than guessing when none is set. The producers FR-NOT-005 names — payment mismatch at M4, printer failure, local-node failure and sync conflict at M5a — do not exist yet. The escalation of a service request is the one critical producer that does, and it is proved end to end.

partial_closures.aspect: transport failures in the dead-letter queue
partial_closures.why: The queue, its reasons, its attempt counting and its safe replay are complete and exercised by three real in-app failures. There is no transport adapter to fail, because outlet-local notices are M5a's, and an adapter seam built here would be an abstraction with one implementation and no second case to prove it right. When a transport exists its failures reach this queue through integration.dead_letter_job(), which is the same door.

partial_closures.aspect: bill, payment, tip and sync in the chain
partial_closures.why: The chain now carries request, cart, table session, order, fulfillment ticket and service request — six of the artifacts FR-INT-014 names, each written by the fold that creates it so a rebuild restores them. Bill, payment and tip are M4's; outlet persistence and sync records are M5a's, recorded separately.

Status and service communications render in the language snapshotted on the table session, with English as the approved fallback, and tests/m3c measures that in a browser. Receipts are the third thing this clause names and they arrive at M4.
